core.text: Hypothesized successful future A depends on the initial rack buffer and bulk replenishment: start trolley B4-B7 at 0, unload and start trolley B8-B11 at 3, unload and start hand B12 at 6, unload B12 at 7. Inspect continuously from 0; predicted completions B1-B8 at 1-8, B9 at 10, B10-B12 at 11-13. Four-carrier unloads fit at 3 and 6. Transfer occupies seven minutes, inspection thirteen.

Closest rival successful future B depends on regular single-carrier arrivals: hand B4-B12 in consecutive trips starting 0-8, unloading 1-9; use the same continuous inspection sequence. Predicted transfer occupation is nine minutes with no blocked unload, correct releases twelve by 13. Lower rack accumulation is a different dependency, but does not outrank a complete seven-minute transfer success.

Backcasting both futures locates the first causal divergence at boundary 0: select a four-carrier trolley trip or hand B4. Present probe: execute A with inspection starting B1 at 0; record each boundary through 3, then continue its stated sequence through 13. A predicts source unload counts 0,0,4 at 1,2,3; the hand rival predicts 1,2,3. Check rack capacity and clerk intervals directly; the rival trajectory is a finite-model counterfactual, not a second observed trial.

residue.text: Defeat A if the first batch cannot unload at 3, inspection idles, any release lacks ten brackets and its completed seal at 13, or transfer occupation reaches nine minutes against the predicted hand success. Thirteen required inspection minutes leave no idle margin. B9 requires the supplied spare and two-minute correction despite its mark. Count nine transferred carriers separately from twelve releases; both actors retain their roles and no extra resources are available.

These schedules are predictions calculated from synthetic stipulations, not observed executions or a proof of global optimality. B9 discrepancy cause remains unknown. Any later smaller, more frequent replenishment requests are unobserved hypotheses; they cannot change this fixed window or justify invented future resources.

tension.account_a: Bulk replenishment exploiting the initial buffer is preferable because both whole batches fit without interrupting inspection.
tension.account_b: Rival explanation under test: early single arrivals are preferable because batch blocking or supply gaps erase the trolley advantage.
